title: Content as an Asset: How Punjab Kings Can Build an Always-On Media Brand
dek: Every season leaves Punjab Kings with a library of moments. Counting them shows how much raw material an always-on media brand has to work with.
excerpt: Punjab Kings have produced centuries, four-wicket hauls and close finishes across their history. That archive is a content asset; how to monetise it is a media question.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: An Archive of Moments
body: Media brands need a steady supply of stories. For a franchise, the richest supply is its own cricket: the hundreds, the spells and the finishes that fans remember.

Punjab Kings batters have scored {{ev:ca-c}} centuries and their bowlers have taken {{ev:ca-w}} four-wicket hauls. Their matches have produced {{ev:ca-cl}} close finishes and {{ev:ca-so}} super overs.

sections.heading: Always-On, Not Only In-Season
body: That is {{ev:ca-per}} highlight moments a season on these three measures alone. An archive that size can feed anniversary posts, retrospectives and player stories in the months without matches.
The data here identifies the moments; rights to the footage sit with the broadcaster and the league.

sections.heading: Turning Moments Into Media
body: The commercial value of an archive depends on rights, formats and distribution, none of which are in the match data.

sections.heading: What the Warehouse Cannot See
body: The CricField warehouse is ball-by-ball cricket data. It contains no video rights, content performance or audience-engagement data, so it cannot measure the commercial side of this question directly.
Measuring content value would need views, watch time and engagement by post, linked to the moments in this archive.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Index the Archive
body: Punjab Kings have a substantial archive of measurable moments. The first step towards an always-on media brand is to index it by player, opponent and date.
Whether it pays depends on rights and audience data held elsewhere.
